description:
The biggest single gap: fz has no String module. Utf8 (4 fns) is the entire text surface.

Ship class A + B + D (~27 of 34 core functions) plus Elixir's two SMALL self-owned
tables, and put UAX #29 grapheme breaking behind one seam.

  A -- pure byte work (12): starts_with?/2 ends_with?/2 byte_slice/3 replace_prefix/3
       replace_suffix/3 replace_leading/3 replace_trailing/3 trim/2 trim_leading/2
       trim_trailing/2 upcase/2 downcase/2 (:ascii)
  B -- codepoint decode, no tables (6): codepoints/1 next_codepoint/1 valid?/2
       printable?/2 replace_invalid/2 chunk/2
  D -- thin primitive wrappers (9): contains?/2 count/2 split/3 splitter/3 replace/4
       duplicate/2 to_atom/1 to_integer/1,2 to_float/1

ONE primitive unlocks five: multi-pattern binary search (:binary.match/matches/split/
compile_pattern) gives split/3 + splitter/3 + replace/4 + contains?/2 + count/2.

Elixir generates code from Unicode data for exactly TWO things -- case mapping (2,989
codepoints + 103 special casings) and whitespace (25 codepoints, under 100 clauses).
Everything grapheme- and normalization-shaped is delegated to OTP's :unicode_util,
which is ~1MB compiled and grows ~15% per OTP major (825KB @ OTP27 -> 1.03MB @ 28 ->
1.18MB @ 29). Define next_grapheme_size/1 as the single seam, alias it to
next_codepoint/1 initially, and keep the tables in their OWN module so demand-driven
per-module loading actually pays.

DESIGN GOAL to state explicitly: fz owns both halves, so it can guarantee ONE coherent
Unicode version. Elixir cannot -- in a running system its case mapping is Unicode 17
while OTP's grapheme breaking is Unicode 16.

fz is ahead of Elixir on one axis: String.t/codepoint/grapheme are all literally
'binary' in Elixir (pure documentation), while fz already brands binaries
(Utf8.from_bytes!, fz_brand_bitstring_as_utf8). A real String.t brand gives static
guarantees Elixir cannot, and lets fz DELETE the invalid-byte fallback clauses that
clutter Elixir's codepoints/1, valid?/2 and normalize/2.

Blocked on fz-5xp.1 (idiomatic String is multi-clause binary matching) and fz-5xp.3.

comments.text:
SHIPPED at e73c306c6: class A + B + D, 26 functions, byte-identical to Elixir on
all three doors.

WHAT THE TICKET ASKED FOR AND WHAT LANDED:

  A -- pure byte work: starts_with?/2 ends_with?/2 byte_slice/3
       replace_prefix/3 replace_suffix/3 replace_leading/3 replace_trailing/3
       trim/1 trim_leading/1 trim_trailing/1 upcase/1 downcase/1 (:ascii)
  B -- codepoints/1 next_codepoint/1 valid?/1, plus length/1 reverse/1
       first/1 last/1
  D -- contains?/2 count/2 split/2 replace/3 duplicate/2 to_atom/1
       index_of/2 join/2 to_byte_list/1

THE ONE PRIMITIVE THE TICKET PREDICTED WAS NOT NEEDED. It said multi-pattern
binary search (:binary.match/matches/split/compile_pattern) would unlock five
functions. It is not there: fz-5xp.55 and fz-5xp.54 landed first, so a byte
scanner is affordable in fz and split/contains?/count/replace/index_of are
plain recursion. The module declares only byte_size/1 and to_atom/1.

NOT LANDED, and each has its reason:
  * printable?/2, replace_invalid/2, chunk/2 -- the remaining three of class B;
  * splitter/3, to_integer/1,2, to_float/1 -- number parsing, which Json
    already does and should be shared rather than written twice;
  * the grapheme seam and the Unicode case/whitespace tables, which the ticket
    itself stages behind next_grapheme_size/1 in its own module;
  * to_charlist/1 -- charlists are deferred project-wide, so what shipped is
    to_byte_list/1 under an honest name.

Found while writing it: fz-5xp.66 (a closure call inside a bitstring segment
does not compile), and a retracted false finding, fz-5xp.65 -- the runtime
library is include_str!'d, so testing a .fz change without cargo build
exercises the previous library.

COMPLETE except for two items, both recorded here rather than closed over.

LANDED across e73c306c6, ecad7fdb2, d06524450:
  * class A -- all 12
  * class B -- all 6, including replace_invalid/2 and chunk/1, the two that
    reason about invalid UTF-8 rather than assuming it away
  * class D -- 8 of 9
  * plus length/1 reverse/1 first/1 last/1 index_of/2 join/2 to_byte_list/1
  * the SEAM: next_grapheme_size/1, with next_grapheme/1 and graphemes/1
    written against it
  * one of the two small tables: the 25-codepoint Unicode whitespace set, so
    trim/1 works over codepoints and matches Elixir on U+3000

The predicted primitive was NOT needed. The ticket said multi-pattern binary
search would unlock five functions; because fz-5xp.55 and fz-5xp.54 landed
first, split/contains?/count/replace/index_of are plain fz recursion. The module
declares two primitives: byte_size/1 and to_atom/1.

TWO ITEMS REMAIN, and neither is a cut I can make alone:

  1. CASE MAPPING -- Elixir's other small table, 2,989 codepoints plus 103
     special casings, generated from UnicodeData.txt. It needs DATA, not code.
     upcase/1 and downcase/1 are :ascii and say so, and the fixture compares
     against Elixir's :ascii mode so the gap is visible rather than papered
     over. Shipping it means vendoring or generating from a Unicode source,
     which is a decision about what fz carries.

  2. splitter/3 -- returns a Stream in Elixir, and fz has no Stream to return.

Both are visible in the fixture's absence rather than hidden in the module.
Awaiting a call on whether either belongs in this ticket or its own.

DONE. Class A + B + D, the grapheme seam, and both tables.

Case mapping is FULL Unicode, matching Elixir's default mode, with the table in
the runtime rather than in fz source -- a measured decision recorded on
fz-5xp.68 and authorized by the user. The whitespace table did land in fz
source, because 25 codepoints is 25 clauses.

splitter/3 is split out to fz-5xp.71 (needs a Stream), authorized by the user.

The ticket's predicted primitive was never needed: it expected multi-pattern
binary search to unlock five functions, and because fz-5xp.55 and fz-5xp.54
landed first, split/contains?/count/replace/index_of are plain fz recursion.
The module declares four primitives -- byte_size/1, to_atom/1, and the two
casing ones -- and everything else is fz over binaries.

title: String core, staged behind a grapheme seam
